paper_summary: Book chapter (Altenaiji, Schleyer and Zhao, 2012, 'Composites and Their Properties', Chapter 19, InTech) reviewing the characterisation of aluminium matrix syntactic foams (metal matrix with hollow or porous ceramic micro-spheres) under static and dynamic loading. It surveys fabrication (stir casting and infiltration casting), porosity relations, the effect of micro-sphere size, wall-thickness-to-radius ratio (t/R), volume fraction and matrix alloy on compressive strength and failure mode, and the test methods used (quasi-static compression, drop weight, Charpy/Izod, split Hopkinson pressure bar and gas gun). The authors report their own SHPB specimen data (Table 1) and ANSYS finite element modelling of a 20 mm cube under 100 kN, and note that dynamic compression gives 10-30% higher peak strength than quasi-static and that Young's modulus increases with relative particle wall thickness.

extraction_notes:
This is a REVIEW book chapter (InTech, 'Composites and Their Properties', Ch. 19) and is overwhelmingly qualitative. It is on-topic (aluminium matrix syntactic foams = metal matrix with hollow/porous ceramic micro-spheres) but contains almost no tabulated property numbers, so the harvest is small (6 records) and low-confidence.

Records 1-4 are the authors' own SHPB experiments from Table 1 (specimens SHPB #2, #3, #4, #6). Table 1 lists ONLY specimen mass, pre/post length, pre/post average width and striker velocity - no stress, strength, modulus or energy value is tabulated for any of them, so every property field is null and the geometry is preserved in test.specimen_notes. Post-test compressive strain was deliberately NOT computed from the pre/post lengths: the schema's strain_at_failure means strain at failure/peak, whereas the post-test length change is the permanent deformation after fragmentation (specimens #3 and #6 lost 70-83% of their mass), so the two are not the same quantity. Specimen density was likewise not computed, because the cross-sectional shape behind 'Avg. Width' is never stated.

Records 5-6 are SECONDARY, quoted by the authors from Kiser, He and Zok (1999): compressive strength 70 MPa at t/R = 0.12 and 230 MPa at t/R = 0.48. UNIT/DEFINITION CONVERSION: the chapter reports the wall-thickness-to-radius ratio t/R, whereas the schema field particle_wall_thickness_ratio is eta = inner/outer radius. Equation 4 of the chapter, rho_o = f(1 - t/R)^3, establishes that (1 - t/R) is exactly the inner/outer radius ratio, so eta = 1 - 0.12 = 0.88 and eta = 1 - 0.48 = 0.52 were entered. The matrix alloy, particle grade, volume fraction and processing route of the cited Kiser study are not restated in this chapter, so process_route is 'other' and those fields are null.

process_route was set to 'other' for all records: the chapter describes both stir casting and (pressure) infiltration casting as the two routes for metal matrix syntactic foams, but never states which was used for its own SHPB specimens. Similarly particle_type was set to 'ceramic_hollow' because the chapter defines these foams as metal matrices with 'hollow or porous ceramic particles' but does not state which type its own specimens used - this is the single largest uncertainty in records 1-4.

Deliberately NOT extracted:
- Figures 4, 5, 9, 10 and 12 (stress-strain curves for AlF25 / Alf75 / Alf250 and for Al7075-75 / al 6082-75, SHPB curves for Tests 2/3/4, and kinetic energy vs. depth of penetration). No numeric values are stated in the text or a table for these curves; only axis ranges survive OCR, so per the extraction rules nothing was read off the plots.
- All purely relative statements, which carry no absolute value: 'the compressive strength of al7075-t is double that of al 6082-T'; al 7075 gives 'approximately double' the strength of pure aluminium (Balch & Dunand, 2006); yield strength under dynamic loading '~ 45-60% higher' than quasi-static (Dou et al., 2007); 'two had 10%-30% higher plateau stress' (Zhang & Zhao, 2007); 'Dynamic compression testing showed a 10-30% increase in peak strength compared to the quasi-static results' (Balch et al., 2005).
- Non-foam apparatus numbers: SHPB steel bars (1000 mm x 20 mm, E = 207 GPa, wave speed 5890 m/s, Poisson 0.29), the dynamic load factor 1.77, and the gas gun (12 mm steel spheres up to 620 m/s).
- The ANSYS FE model (100 kN applied to a 20 x 20 x 20 mm aluminium matrix syntactic foam cube, SOLID186/SOLID187 and SURF154 elements, multi-linear isotropic hardening). No output property value is reported - only the qualitative findings that Young's modulus increases with relative wall thickness and that peak stress occurs on the inner surface of the particles - so no 'model' record could be created. The 250 MPa nominal stress implied by 100 kN over a 20 x 20 mm face is an applied load, not a measured or predicted material property, and was not recorded.

No test temperature is stated anywhere, so temperature_c is null throughout rather than assumed to be room temperature.
